chapter: Life in New York in the 1940s
title: Not drinking or smoking; New York's temptations
summary: Edison says Lester and Billie did not drink or smoke at first, and how fast New York was.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: He didn't smoke a cigarette. Didn't smoke at all.

Didn't drink, no. When he first left Kansas City, he had an old cob pipe he used to hold in his mouth but he never even had tobacco for it. And Lady Day was the same way. I knew her when she didn't -- she didn't even smoke a cigarette, you know.

And well, you know how New York is. New York is so fast you've got to have a lot of willpower to stay within the bounds of your teachings, you know. Like most kids, most musicians that have ended up in New York, they've had the good background but the environment in New York, New York was so fast, you know.

A lot of the musicians and a lot of people not in the music world get to New York and think that New York owes them something. And they all tried to prove something in New York. And they end up, you know, in the tarpits.
